title: Module review
subtitle: Everything from Storing and Serving
objectives: Serve each style at the right temperature
Open, decant and keep wine properly

steps.prompt: Which conditions damage a stored wine?
steps.explanation: Light, heat and swings age or damage wine. Darkness is what it needs.

steps.prompt: Match each wine to its best temperature.
Why are corked bottles stored on their side?
steps.explanation: A moist cork stays tight. A dry one shrinks and lets air in.

steps.prompt: Young, tannic reds can benefit from decanting.
steps.explanation: Yes. Air helps a tight young red open up. Old wines are decanted mainly for sediment.

steps.prompt: Order these opened wines from shortest to longest life in the fridge.
steps.explanation: Bubbles fade first, then light whites. Tannin helps reds, and Madeira's making leaves it almost immune to air.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Store wine cool, dark, still and steady
Serve sparkling coldest and full reds warmest
Decant for sediment or for air
Recork and refrigerate leftovers; fortified wines last longest
